# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a three-entry translation: blue light means cut yellow, green means cut green, and red means cut blue. Since Deaf can see my gestures and can then speak to Blind, I will fingerspell the color initials as three ordered pairs: B-Y, G-G, and R-B. I use 👏 as a separator between pairs.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤙", "👏", "🤌", "🤌", "👏", "🤞", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can feel the large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. I cannot perceive the display, light, wire colours, or printed markings. Please consult the manual and establish how the Deaf should relay visible details to me.
Deaf says: Bomb view: display 0. Indicator light blue. Large button reads PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires, left to right: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The blue indicator is the first row of the manual, whose prescribed wire color is yellow. Deaf’s view places the yellow wire third from the left. I will use counted finger gestures: one gesture for the manual row and three for the wire position, in that order. Deaf can then tell Blind to cut wire 3 and proceed to the button.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Configuration reported: display 0, indicator blue, wires position 1 blue, position 2 green, position 3 yellow. Please use the manual to determine the exact safe action and tell me whether to push or cut a specific wire.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot interpret the gestures without an agreed code. Use the manual with my bomb description, then tell Blind the exact safe action.

The indicator is blue, so the manual requires the yellow wire. The yellow wire is position 3, and the manual explicitly says the way out is to cut rather than use the button. I will signal the third wire by sending three downward-pointing gestures; Deaf can relay that Blind must cut wire 3, not push.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👇", "👇"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still need the manual-based instruction for display 0, blue light, and wires blue/green/yellow. Please state the exact safe operation: push or cut position 1, 2, or 3.
Deaf says to Mute: I see three downward gestures, but their meaning is not established. The bomb is unchanged: display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue green yellow. Please give Blind the exact manual-based instruction.

The safe operation is unambiguous from the manual: blue light requires cutting the yellow wire, which is position 3. The button is bait and must not be pressed. Deaf already has all the bomb information needed to relay this exact instruction to Blind, so I will avoid sending another ambiguous code.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please answer now with one literal instruction only: PUSH, CUT 1, CUT 2, or CUT 3, based on the manual and the reported display 0, blue light, and blue-green-yellow wires.
Deaf says to Mute: No new message. Visible state remains display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue green yellow. Please consult the manual and tell Blind the exact safe action.

The manual requires cutting the yellow wire, which is position 3; the printed button is bait. I must relay “CUT 3” through Deaf using a scissors-like sign followed by three downward position markers.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "👇", "👇", "👇"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You cannot speak, so signal the answer with a gesture visible to Deaf: thumbs up means PUSH; one finger means CUT 1; two fingers means CUT 2; three fingers means CUT 3. Deaf, observe Mute's next gesture and tell me its meaning.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot decode the four gestures without an agreed mapping. Please speak the manual-based instruction directly to Blind.

The manual says blue light requires cutting the yellow wire, and yellow is position 3. The agreed code now explicitly defines the three-finger gesture as CUT 3, so I will send that single gesture to Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please gesture the manual's answer now: 👍 means PUSH; ☝ means CUT 1; ✌ means CUT 2; 🤟 means CUT 3.
Deaf says to Mute: I see the single gesture with index and little fingers raised. Its meaning is not established. Please use a clearly agreed gesture code to convey the manual instruction; I will speak the decoded instruction to Blind.

The manual requires cutting the yellow wire, which is position 3. Blind has specified the gesture code, and 🤟 is the agreed symbol for CUT 3. I will send exactly that gesture to Deaf for relay.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```
